agentCan: Implement the PKCE authorization-code flow and token handling
Prepare integration properties (tagline, homepage, logo, support email)
Build reach-discovery calls (List Bases; userId-and-scopes) so the UI reflects live grants

approval.cost: No developer fee stated; help center lists OAuth integrations as available on all plan types
approval.trigger: No review. The developer docs describe no Airtable review, approval, or marketplace-listing step for OAuth integrations. The only distribution gate is paperwork: 'the Privacy policy URL and Terms of service URL must be provided before sharing your OAuth integration with other users; if you have not provided them, other users will not be able to authorize your integration', and the distribution step adds the support email to that list. Missing fields surface as an access_denied authorization error. Separately, a user's own enterprise can restrict them from using your integration (also an access_denied cause).

blockers.detail: 'You have reached the maximum access authorizations for this integration': each user can hold at most 20 authorizations for your integration and must revoke one before authorizing again. (There is no limit on how many different integrations a user can authorize.)
blockers.howToClear: Design reconnect flows to reuse or revoke stale authorizations; surface the cap in your error handling.
blockers.title: 20 authorizations per user per integration

blockers.detail: 'Airtable does not store a copy of your client secret': lose it and regenerating is the only remedy. Worse, 'generating a client secret is potentially a breaking change: if you are already sending existing authorization requests, they will fail until you start sending this client secret.' And the token endpoint flips its rule on whether a secret exists: Basic auth header required if one exists, forbidden if none does.
blockers.howToClear: Decide the secret posture before launch; store the secret in a vault at generation time.
blockers.title: The client-secret one-way door

blockers.detail: Per the official help center: no API endpoint exists to revoke a refresh token programmatically; tokens are revoked if reused after rotation, retried after the duplicate-refresh grace period, or sent with incorrect client credentials, after which the user must re-authorize.
blockers.howToClear: Persist rotated tokens atomically and never retry a refresh with a stale token.
blockers.title: Refresh-token reuse revokes the grant

sources.label: Third-party integrations via OAuth (help center: 20-authorization cap, refresh invalidation)

Whether Airtable offers any optional public listing/marketplace for OAuth integrations (not described in the docs read; documented distribution is direct authorization links).

alternatives: Personal access tokens (single-user; the docs direct multi-user products to OAuth integrations)
flavor.recommended: An OAuth integration registered at airtable.com/create/oauth, authorization code flow with PKCE (S256)
flavor.why: Registration yields a client_id; a client secret is optional ('You should generate a client secret if you will be issuing token requests from a server'). Authorization is two-dimensional: scopes (what actions) plus resources (which bases/workspaces the user picks on the consent screen). The docs are plain: 'If you are building an Airtable integration for your product or for many different users, you will need to create an OAuth integration.'

humanMust: Register the integration and configure its properties in the UI
Generate the client secret (server-side apps) and vault it immediately; it is not recoverable
Provide the Privacy policy URL, Terms of service URL, and support email before other users can authorize
name: Airtable
nuances: Grant codes are single-use, even on failure: 'Individual code values can only be used once, even if the request fails.' Token exchange must happen within 10 minutes of the authorization request.

Scope pre-registration: you can only request scopes already selected on the integration; anything else (empty, duplicated, unregistered) returns invalid_scope. Scopes are granular and tiered: basic scopes for all users, enterprise-member scopes, and enterprise-admin scopes (SCIM, audit logs) most users simply cannot grant.

Consent is resource-picking, and grants move: a token's reach is granted scopes intersected with granted bases, and 'these may change at any time' (user edits the grant, or loses/re-gains collaborator access to a base). Discover current reach via List Bases and the userId-and-scopes endpoint. Revoking an authorization kills everything granted through that token at once.
Redirect mismatch fails silently: if redirect_uri doesn't match one registered for the client_id, 'you will not receive an error response'.
Tokens are opaque: 'do not rely on tokens having a particular length or format'; format changes are not considered breaking changes.
Refresh tokens are automatically invalidated after 60 days of inactivity (help center).
prerequisites: A redirect URL (HTTPS required except localhost)
Privacy policy URL, Terms of service URL, and support email (required before other users can authorize)

steps.detail: At airtable.com/create/oauth choose 'Register new OAuth integration': give it a unique name and a valid redirect URL, click Register integration (both changeable later).
steps.title: Register the OAuth integration

steps.detail: On the management page set the permission scopes the integration may request, plus tagline, homepage URL, logo, and support email. All fields are shown to users on the authorization dialog.
steps.title: Configure properties and scopes

steps.detail: From the management page, 'Generate client secret', and vault it immediately: Airtable does not store a copy. Adding a secret later is a breaking change for in-flight authorization requests.
steps.title: (Server-side apps) Generate a client secret

steps.detail: GET airtable.com/oauth2/v1/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri (exact match, HTTPS except localhost), response_type=code, scope (space-delimited, at least one, every scope Airtable-defined and pre-selected on the integration), state (cryptographically generated opaque string), and the PKCE pair (code_challenge, S256). On the consent screen the user also picks resources: specific bases, workspaces (all current and future bases), all workspaces, or (enterprise admins) an entire enterprise.
steps.title: Build the authorization request (PKCE)

steps.detail: POST form-encoded to airtable.com/oauth2/v1/token within 10 minutes of the authorization request. If the integration has a client secret, an Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret) header is required; if it has none, that header is forbidden. Codes are single-use even if the request fails.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: Call the API with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. Before sharing the integration with other users, complete the Privacy policy URL, Terms of service URL, and support email, or other users' authorizations fail with access_denied.
steps.title: Call the API; complete distribution fields

tagline: No review and no approval, but the token mechanics have teeth: a 20-authorization cap per user, single-use codes that die even on failed exchanges, refresh reuse that revokes the grant, and a client secret Airtable cannot give back to you.

time.active: ~20 min of configuration + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day; no review stands in front of users
